name: EmpRoster
author: Alif

sections.description:
EmpRoster is a self-hosted WordPress plugin for managing staff schedules. Everything is stored in your own database — no external APIs, no SaaS dependencies, no per-seat pricing.

Core features:

  • Visual weekly and monthly roster views
  • Shift creation with direct assignment or open-slot mode
  • Clock in / clock out attendance with break tracking
  • Leave requests with manager approval workflow
  • Weekly availability management per employee
  • Shift swap requests between employees
  • Payroll calculations with optional tax
  • Daily labour budget tracking
  • Email notifications for key events
  • Frontend employee portal via shortcodes
  • Profile Mode to restrict employee WordPress logins
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/
  2. Activate via Plugins > Installed Plugins
  3. Navigate to EmpRoster > Settings to configure
  4. Assign the Roster Manager role to your scheduling staff
sections.faq:
Do I need to pay monthly?

No. EmpRoster uses annual licences, not subscriptions. One payment per year.

Is my data stored on your servers?

No. All data stays on your WordPress server. The plugin has no SaaS dependency.

Can employees access without logging into WordPress admin?

Yes. Five frontend shortcode pages let employees view shifts, clock in/out, submit leave, and set availability without accessing WP Admin. Profile Mode can block employee logins entirely.
sections.changelog:
2.8.12

  • Changed: Pay rates and earnings are no longer part of this package. A packaging error in earlier builds left the pay-rate field and the timesheet earnings columns switched on here even though they belong to a separate product; that code is now removed from this build rather than shipped switched off. If you used pay rates, the pay-rate box on staff records and the Pay Rate / Gross Earnings columns on the timesheet will no longer appear.
  • Your data is not deleted. Any pay rates you already entered stay stored against each staff record, untouched. Nothing is erased, reset, or zeroed, and the figures reappear exactly as they were if the site later moves to a product that includes payroll.
  • Fixed: A staff record could still accept a pay-rate value sent directly to the server even though no screen offered the field. That write is no longer performed here.
  • Note: Everything else EmpRoster does — shifts, the roster, staff records, timesheets and hours — works in full with no usage limits. Features belonging to separate products have no code in this package at all.

2.8.10

  • Added: An “Upgrade” item in the EmpRoster menu. It is a plain link to the EmpRoster website — there is no page behind it, and it reads nothing about your site.
  • Note: Nothing in this plugin is restricted, reduced, or switched off. Everything EmpRoster does here — shifts, the roster, staff records, timesheets — works in full with no usage limits. The features named on that page are part of separate products and have no code in this package at all.
  • Housekeeping: The new page is packaged into this build only and does not change any existing screen or behaviour.

2.8.7

  • Simplified staff management so that account-level administration is handled entirely through WordPress’s built-in Administrator role, removing an internal manager permission tier that duplicated WordPress’s own capability system.
  • Removed unused settings and internal scaffolding left over from that simplification.

2.8.6

  • Improved: The free build no longer carries leftover premium code paths. Unreachable credentialed “welcome” and “account reset” emails, their login-link buttons, and a manager capability re-grant are now removed from the package during build rather than shipped inert.
  • Security: All remaining supervisor-tier logic is stripped from the free build. Supervisors are a premium role; on a site downgraded from premium, a leftover supervisor account is now treated exactly like a regular employee — no elevated staff visibility, pay visibility, pending-request counts, admin Staff menu, or API access remains for it.
  • Housekeeping: These changes affect packaging of the free build only. Behaviour for regular free users is unchanged, and the premium build is unchanged.

2.8.4

  • Fixed: Removed a redundant translation-loading call that triggered a “function was called incorrectly” notice on WordPress 6.7 and later. Translations are unaffected — WordPress loads them automatically from the plugin’s own language folder.
  • Improved: Added a translator note to the fallback name shown when a staff account has no display name, so it can be translated correctly.
  • Housekeeping: The distributed packages no longer contain internal development documentation or the project’s code-analysis configuration. Nothing that affects how the plugin runs was removed.

2.8.1

  • Improved: The free build now ships only the features it actually offers. Leave management, leave balances, and attendance are no longer part of the free package at all — their settings, wizard steps, shortcodes, and admin pages are removed during packaging rather than shipped and hidden.
  • Improved: Existing installs upgrading to this release have any now-unused plugin pages moved to Draft instead of being left as broken links. Upgrading later restores them automatically, so no page or URL is lost.
  • Improved: The free build’s admin JavaScript no longer carries unreachable code for features it does not include, including the staff role selector’s unavailable roles.
  • Improved: Admin styles and scripts are now registered under consistent empr handles and load in a defined order, avoiding clashes with other plugins.
  • Housekeeping: Clarified code comments throughout the admin and build layers. No change in behaviour on either build.

2.8.0

  • Complete architectural rework of the free build to remove all plan-tier awareness. No plan checks, tier limits, upgrade prompts, or locked-feature code remain anywhere in the free package (PHP, JavaScript, or CSS).
  • Fixed a data-loss bug where saving Settings could silently overwrite stored values for fields not shown on the current page.
  • Fixed a fatal error that could occur in specific configurations due to a duplicate method definition.
  • Various security hardening around staff account management.

2.7.6

  • Improved: The free (WordPress.org) build now also strips premium-only styling and tier vocabulary from the distributed package. The upgrade prompt, plan-tier colour system, and upgrade card/button/pill styles are removed from the stylesheets during packaging (rather than shipping unused), and code comments no longer reference paid tiers by name. Behaviour is unchanged on both the free and premium builds.
  • Housekeeping: Updated the “Tested up to” WordPress version.

2.7.5

  • Improved: The free (WordPress.org) build’s admin JavaScript is now free of premium code at the source level. Every plan-gated conditional, tier check, and upgrade prompt has been moved out of the shared application core into a premium-only module, so the distributed free package’s app.js contains no plan or tier logic at all — previously it shipped that logic inert. The build now verifies the packaged file carries no plan vocabulary before publishing. Behaviour is unchanged on both the free and premium builds.

2.7.0

  • New: Every plugin page — roster, shifts, staff, leave, attendance, analytics, settings, and the frontend employee portal — is now fully usable on phones and tablets. Layouts reflow to a single column, wide tables stack into readable cards, modals and toolbars fit small screens, and form fields no longer trigger the zoom-in behaviour on mobile Safari. Desktop is unchanged.
  • Fixed: Saving Settings no longer wipes stored values for fields that were not shown on the form. Previously, any setting hidden from the current view — for example leave entitlements, labour budget amounts, penalty rates, or manager settings access — could be silently reset to a default on every save. Only fields actually present on the page are now written; everything else is left untouched.
  • Improved: The free (WordPress.org) build now excludes premium-only code from the distributed package rather than only blocking it at runtime, so the free build is leaner and cannot reach premium-only logic. The premium build is unchanged.

2.6.7

  • Fixed: On the free build, a dev/testing configuration could register the premium-only account-reset action even though its handler is stripped from the package, which would cause a fatal error if that action were ever dispatched. Registration now skips any action whose handler is absent from the build, matching the existing safeguard used for analytics. Customer installs were never affected; the premium build is unchanged.

2.6.6

  • Security: Manager-tier accounts can now only be managed by a WordPress administrator. A roster manager can no longer create another manager, promote anyone to manager, change an existing manager’s role, change their own role, or reset or deactivate a manager account. This closes a privilege-escalation and manager-on-manager lockout path. Managing employee and supervisor accounts is unchanged.
  • New: Login Logs can now be exported to CSV. Choose a period (today, this week, this month, this year, or a custom date range) and download all matching entries — including employee name, role, email, login date and time, IP address, browser/device, and login status. The export respects the same access permissions as the Login Logs view and streams large datasets efficiently. (Professional plan.)

2.6.3

  • Improved: The free (WordPress.org) build now fully excludes premium-only leave and attendance code from the distributed files. Leave submission and approval, and employee clock in / clock out, are stripped during packaging rather than only blocked at runtime, and all remaining free code paths are plan-guarded. The free build is leaner and cannot reach premium-only logic; the premium build is unchanged.
  • Fixed: On the free build, the dashboard data endpoint no longer attempts to read time-tracking data (a Starter-plan feature), preventing an error when premium attendance code is absent. Paid plans are unaffected.

2.6.2

  • Security: Editing a staff member can no longer change a WordPress administrator’s email address through the roster. Because email addresses drive password-reset flows, this closes a potential account-takeover path. Administrator names can still be updated when the administrator is included in the roster.
  • Fixed: Reactivating a staff member now fully validates the target account before any changes are made, so requests that are correctly rejected (for example, targeting an administrator or a non-roster account) no longer alter the account’s active status.

2.6.0

  • Plan access: Leave management (requests, approvals, and balances) and employee self-service attendance (clock in / clock out and attendance history) now require the Starter plan or above. Access is enforced in the interface and on the server, so these actions are blocked for Free installs rather than only hidden.
  • Improved: The free (WordPress.org) build now ships only the handlers it needs — premium-only methods are stripped during packaging and all call sites are safely guarded, so the free build is cleaner and unaffected by premium-only code. The premium build is unchanged.

2.5.20

  • Fixed: The free (WordPress.org) build now strips the plugin-icon update helper entirely during packaging, so the site_transient_update_plugins references no longer appear anywhere in the distributed file. This clears a false positive from the WordPress.org plugin scanner. The premium build is unaffected and keeps the helper.

2.5.19

  • New: Dashboard cards now have a small “i” info icon in the top-right corner. Hover (desktop) or tap (mobile/tablet) to see a short explanation of what each metric means, how it is calculated, and the timeframe it covers — across both the KPI cards and the analytics panels.
  • Fixed: In the free (WordPress.org) build, the plugin-icon update filters are now only registered when the Freemius SDK is present, so the free build no longer references the update-transient hooks when the SDK is excluded.

2.5.17

  • Security: Password resets are now restricted to roster roles only — WordPress administrators and users without a roster role can no longer trigger a reset through the roster, closing an unintended access path.
  • Security: Custom location entries saved in Settings are now individually sanitised, keeping only valid names and colours.
  • New: Refreshed styling for the Upgrade page (Free build) for a cleaner, more consistent layout.
  • Improved: Frontend shortcodes renamed from emp_roster_* to empr_* for naming consistency. Existing pages are migrated automatically, so older shortcodes keep working.
  • Improved: Internal database table references now resolve through the WordPress table prefix, improving compatibility on installs that use a non-standard prefix.

2.5.11

  • New: Timesheets earnings columns now break down pay for clearer payroll reporting. The “Earnings” column is renamed “Gross Earnings”, and when tax is enabled under Settings two additional columns appear — “Tax Amount” (showing the configured rate) and “Net Earnings” (Gross minus Tax). All pay-related columns stay hidden until “Reveal Pay” is pressed, then show together, and respect supervisor pay-visibility restrictions across daily, weekly, monthly, and yearly views, detail modals, and CSV exports.
  • Improved: The employee shift detail modal now clearly shows the shift’s break length (e.g. “30 min” or “No break”) when viewing a shift.
  • Improved: Open Shift Requests no longer use a separate “Completed” status. An approved request stays labelled “Approved” for the life of the record instead of flipping to “Completed” once the shift ends, keeping status badges, history, and filters consistent. Existing approved requests display as “Approved” automatically.

2.5.10

  • New: Daily Budget Target by Day (Professional+). A new toggle under Settings > Payroll > Budgeting reveals seven per-weekday budget target fields (Monday–Sunday). When enabled, each weekday’s target drives the colour-coded labour-cost comparison independently across the week and month roster views, the analytics Budget panel, and the dashboard summaries. Disabling the toggle resets all weekday targets to 0 and restores the single Daily Budget Target behaviour.
  • New: Analytics “Today” reporting tab, alongside This Week, This Month, and This Year. Each tab now shows the active reporting period as a clear date label in the analytics header (e.g. “5 June 2026”, “1 Jun 2026 – 7 Jun 2026”, “June 2026”, “2026”) that updates instantly when switching tabs and stays consistent across every analytics widget.
  • New: Drag-and-drop reorderable Analytics cards. Managers and supervisors can reorder the analytics cards by dragging or using the on-card Left/Right/Up/Down controls. The layout saves per user and persists across refresh, logout, and devices, with a safe fallback to the default order (Hours & Overtime, Budget, Payroll Estimate, Leave) if saved data is invalid.
  • Improved: Cleaner dashboard KPI cards — “Hours This Week” and “Upcoming Shifts” are now labelled “My Hours This Week” and “My Upcoming Shifts”, the hours card shows a simpler “This Week” sub-label, and KPI cards no longer overflow when displaying large values.

2.5.8

  • Fixed the plugin icon showing as a broken/404 image on the Dashboard > Updates screen on symlinked hosting (e.g. Bitnami). The Freemius plugin_icon filter built the icon path from dirname(__FILE__), which on symlinked installs resolves to a realpath (e.g. /bitnami/wordpress/…) that does not start with WP_CONTENT_DIR or WP_PLUGIN_DIR, so Freemius fell back to the theme-root URL and produced a malformed 404 URL. empr_fs_plugin_icon() now anchors the path to WP_PLUGIN_DIR so Freemius always resolves a correct plugin URL.

2.5.7

  • Fixed the plugin icon rendering as a broken/blank image on the Dashboard > Updates screen when WordPress admin is accessed over HTTPS. The update-plugins transient is often built during wp-cron over HTTP (when siteurl is http), which stored an http:// icon URL that browsers block as mixed content on an https admin page. The empr_attach_plugin_icon() function now runs the icon URL through set_url_scheme() so it always matches the scheme of the current request (https on SSL admin pages, http otherwise), preventing the mixed-content block.

2.5.6

  • Strengthened the plugin icon display: the empr_attach_plugin_icon() function now hooks both the read and write update-transient filters at priority 20 (after Freemius), unconditionally stamping the icon onto the transient to reliably override any empty, missing, or stale icon entries, ensuring the EmpRoster icon always displays on the Dashboard > Updates and Plugins screens instead of the generic grey placeholder.

2.5.5

  • Fixed the plugin icon not displaying on the Dashboard > Updates and Plugins screens. Implemented a new empr_attach_plugin_icon() function that hooks into site_transient_update_plugins to stamp the plugin icon directly onto the update transient, fixing both fresh and already-cached transients without requiring manual refresh.

  • Timesheets: the “Leave (Days)” column now includes all approved leave types (Annual, Sick, Personal, Unpaid, Other) in the total, previously only Annual and Sick were counted.
  • Timesheets: leave day numbers now render in default text color instead of the brand color.
  • Employees are now restricted from creating leave requests or shift swap requests for past dates; today and future dates are allowed. Managers and administrators can still record retroactive requests.
  • Fixed the plugin icon not appearing on the Dashboard > Updates and Plugins screens for the self-hosted Freemius updater.
